briefing.hook: At 11:47 PM, the station's final live broadcast cut to static, and host Elias Voss vanished from the control room before the closing signal could finish.
briefing.context: The door to Studio 3 was locked from the inside. Elias's headset was still live, but the waveforms show the signal was routed through the archive switcher instead of the desk board.
briefing.tension: The station manager says it was a technical fault. The engineers insist nobody else had access to the archive room. The broadcast log disagrees with both.
briefing.objective: Find out who disrupted the broadcast, how they did it, and what Elias was trying to say before the signal died.

truth.incident: Mara Vale, the archive engineer, intercepted Elias's live broadcast after discovering he was about to expose a licensing fraud tied to the station owner. She rerouted the signal through the archive switcher, locked Studio 3 from the inside, and left Elias trapped long enough to steal his notes and censor the final message. Elias was not abducted; he was silenced in plain sight.

timeline.description: Elias receives a call about an unsigned licensing invoice.
Mara enters the archive corridor with a maintenance pass.
The broadcast feed shifts from Studio 3 to the archive switcher.
The program cuts to static; Elias disappears from the control room.

criticalFacts: The broadcast was routed through the archive switcher, not the desk board.
Studio 3 was locked from the inside after the feed changed.
Mara had archive-room access and a maintenance pass.
Elias was about to expose station fraud.
His notes were removed before the room was opened.
importantSecondaryTruths: Jonah lied about hearing the signal fail because he was asleep in the control booth.
Tess saw Mara in the archive corridor but assumed she was doing routine maintenance.
The station manager knew about the fraudulent invoices and tried to bury the story.

questions.text: Where were you when the broadcast cut out?

variants.text: I was moving between systems. The live feed was unstable.
On mic, until the static hit.
In Studio 3, waiting for the closing cue.
At the console, where I was supposed to be.
I never left the control room.
I may have nodded off for a moment.
In the booth, watching the floor.
Moving between the booth and corridor.
I was nearby when the cut happened.

statements.canonicalMeaning: Mara says she was in the archive, not Studio 3.
Tess says the archive corridor light was on at 23:31.

contradictions.description: The broadcast path changed before static, which cannot happen if the desk board simply failed.
The studio was locked from inside after the signal changed, implying whoever caused it had to move through the archive corridor first.

redHerrings.surfaceSuspicion: He altered the incident log and looked guilty.
redHerrings.actualReason: He was covering an embarrassing lapse in attention.

solutionPaths.name: Signal path
solutionPaths.description: Routing record -> internal lock -> Mara access -> admission.

solutionPaths.name: Motive path
solutionPaths.description: Fraud trail -> Elias's notes -> Mara access -> admission.

options.label: The broadcast was hijacked to hide a cover-up.
A technical fault caused the failure.
An outside intruder caused the cut.
To cover up a panic response.
Rerouted the feed, locked the studio, and stole the notes.

reveal.headline: The last broadcast was silenced from inside the station.
narrative: Mara discovered Elias was about to expose a licensing fraud tied to station management.
She rerouted the live feed through the archive switcher before the closing cue.
Studio 3 was locked from the inside while Elias was trapped long enough for her to remove his notes.
Jonah's log tampering hid his own lapse, but not the routing change.
Tess and the signal printout together show the cut was deliberate, not accidental.

truthBreakdown.fact: The broadcast was rerouted through the archive switcher.
Elias was trying to expose fraud.
